specification.family_title: Commit outcome after a connection or reply failure
specification.title: The connection is terminated after the last write, before COMMIT
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(). The runner terminates that backend from its own connection, and waits until it has gone.
Wait settle_ms, so that the driver can observe the closed connection.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework attempts to commit.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When the connection or PostgreSQL's reply was lost around COMMIT, so that the client never received an acknowledgement of COMMIT, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: Negative control. PDO::commit() returning true is reported as committed, including after a caught unique violation. A thrown commit() is reported as rolled_back. A thrown rollBack() keeps the handle. The next unit continues on that handle when beginTransaction reports an active transaction. ATTR_PERSISTENT is false.

configuration.failed_rollback: handle kept; next beginTransaction may continue on it
configuration.connections: one PDO handle at a time, not a pool

execution.form: PDO::beginTransaction(), prepared inserts against item and uniq, then PDO::commit() or PDO::rollBack(). One connection is held. It is not a pool.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: After the last write, before the framework sends COMMIT.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and its transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: A connection error at COMMIT. No reply to COMMIT can arrive.

knowledge: Known not committed: the session ended before the framework tried to commit, so the driver refused to send COMMIT ("Client has encountered a connection error and is not queryable"). A report of rollback is justified; a report of success is not.

api_outcome.basis: PDO::commit() threw, which the unsafe policy reports as a rollback
api_outcome.contract: The unsafe pdo-control policy reports committed when PDO::commit() returns true, including after a unique violation was caught in the same transaction. It does not read a command tag, and PDO::commit() does not return one. A true return is the success signal. When PDO::commit() throws, the policy reports rolled_back. When the body throws and PDO::rollBack() throws, the policy reports failed and keeps the PDO handle. The next unit calls PDO::beginTransaction(). If that throws "already an active transaction", the policy writes and calls PDO::commit() on the same handle. There is no Connection.setAutoCommit. This is not the JDBC unsafe policy's setAutoCommit(true) call.

error.message: SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 7 FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command server closed the connection unexpectedly This probably means the server terminated abnormally before or while processing the request.
